Presidential Gubernatorial Governor Dauda Lawa
Zamfara State is among the eight states across the federation that fully cleared their inherited pension and gratuity liabilities. This was revealed in a report released by the National Pension Commission (PenCom) last week.
The report titled, ‘Securing every Nigerian’s future: The pension redemption scorecard: before and after,’ was dated 10 November 2026.
The new report, signed by the Director General of PenCom, Omolola Oloworaran, was released in Abuja at the launch of Presidential Pension Security Initiatives.
As at October 2026, according to the report, Zamfara was among the only eight states that fully cleared its share of inherited pension obligations.
Captured under the title, ‘The quiet revolution: States are paying their retirees,’ the seven other states that also cleared their legacy pension backlogs are Lagos, Gombe, Borno, Anambra, Jigawa, Katsina, and Kebbi.
It also said that six other states — Delta, Osun, Ogun, Akwa Ibom, Kaduna, and Oyo — have paid off their pension liabilities by over 80 per cent.
The PenCom report said before President Bola Tinubu’s fiscal reforms, the 36 states owed a combined pension liability exceeding N2 trillion.

In legacy pensions and gratuities, states cleared out of the N2 trillion they inherited.
The pension chief attributed this development to economic and fiscal reforms that improved their capacity to meet retirement obligations.
“President Tinubu’s fiscal reforms expanded the revenues flowing to every State. Governors are turning that fiscal space into dignity for those who served,” the report said.
Governor Dauda Lawal prioritised payment of inherited pension obligations when he came to office on May 29, 2023, by settling over ₦13.6 billion in long-standing gratuity arrears dating back as far as 2011 across Zamfara’s 14 local government areas and state ministries.
This included multi-batch disbursements to thousands of retired civil servants, local government workers, and primary school teachers.
The governor also inaugurated the Zamfara State Pension Reform Committee to build institutional safeguards and prevent future backlogs of unpaid retirement benefits.
